A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, three figures, algorithms, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching proofs and examples relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds, proofs, illustrative matching instances, and a hypothetical batch-learning example. It reports no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. The new two-sided learning discussion reports no experiments, and Section 6 identifies evaluation on real-world datasets as future work.

M1.justification: The duplication, Gale–Shapley, and ETCO procedures are retained. v2 Remark 2 adds optional post-processing that assigns an unused job to its recipient in another supported matching, preserving internal stability. Prescribed duplication and exploration parameters also change in Theorem 5 and Corollary 2.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or test scenarios for empirical training or evaluation. Appendix K's two-sided learning extension is theoretical discussion, not added evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Added discussions of Kong et al. and Zhang and Fang concern theoretical positioning, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. Revisions to duplication counts and exploration lengths are theoretical algorithm prescriptions, not changes to reported experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness tests, or error analyses. Robustness through epsilon-stability is analyzed mathematically in both; the new applicability discussion does not add such tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, measured error bars, or significance tests. The concentration inequalities and confidence bounds used analytically within ETCO are retained.

E6.justification: No measured results are added, removed, or revised. The worked matching examples and four-worker lower-bound utility calculations are retained under relocation and renumbering; revisions to formal guarantees are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: The central bounds and proofs remain. Theorem 5 changes m from ceil(log2 N) to floor(log2 N + 2), and Corollary 2 changes T0 from T/ln T to T/(2 ln T). Theorem 6 strengthens its stated output support from general to internally stable matchings. v2 also reformulates the approximation oracle around an uncertainty set and adds two-sided regret and Pessimal Stable Share formulations in Appendix K.

C1.justification: The OSS approximation and regret-trade-off contributions are retained. v2 additionally claims ex-ante stability in Section 1.3 and Remark 1, and a first instance-independent worker-optimal stable-regret bound in the conclusion. The conclusion also drops v1's equal-number-of-workers-and-jobs qualification when claiming matching upper and lower bounds.

C2.justification: v2 explains why the intermediate-gap regime incurs linear standard regret after Corollary 1. Its conclusion explicitly identifies centralization as a limitation and decentralized learning as unresolved. New Appendix K discusses learning preferences on both sides and leaves achieving sublinear regret with ties for all agents open.

D1.justification: The explicit parameter prescriptions change locally in Theorem 5 and Corollary 2, affecting reproduction of those algorithm configurations. The full ETCO pseudocode is retained; its inlined mean-update equation was already supplied in v1. Neither PDF adds code, data-access, or hardware information.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 adds Kong et al. (2025) and distinguishes its pessimistic benchmark. Appendix K adds comparison with Zhang and Fang (2024), while Remark 3 adds combinatorial-bandit lower-bound references. The master-preference-list reference to Irving et al. (2008) is removed. The central positioning around OSS fairness remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution summary, technical overview, and conclusion are extensively rewritten and condensed. Substantial main-text proofs move into organized appendices, examples are reordered, and the appendix structure is extensively reorganized. These changes substantially alter the narrative while preserving most mathematics.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS formatting with redesigned title and author blocks, typography, and display placement. Figures 1–3 retain their content but move into Appendices B and C. Algorithm 2 moves to Appendix D; the abstract ETCO box is removed, while the retained full pseudocode becomes Algorithm 3 in Appendix E.

improvement.justification: The clearer contribution summary, organized proof appendices, updated research positioning, and explicit applicability limits provide a modest overall improvement. Theorem 5's revised duplication count also agrees with its proof. Gains in precision remain limited: Theorem 6 and the batch-learning example retain the earlier count, and the conclusion's bound-matching claim loses v1's equal-market-size qualification.
